newsitem.title: italy: SOCCER-AC MILAN, WITH BAGGIO, LOOK TO GO TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AC MILAN, WITH BAGGIO, LOOK TO GO TOP.

text.p: Champions AC Milan could go top of the Italian League if they win at Roma on Saturday, but their stay there may be short.
Current league leaders Juventus play Vicenza on Sunday as the league programme swings back into action after a 10-day break for World Cup matches.
If Juve win as expected, they should be back in first place by the end of the weekend.
Milan, who have not lost to Rome in the league for more than 10 years, travel without suspended Croat Zvonimir Boban and injured Yugoslavian Dejan Savicevic.
Roberto Baggio, the league's most costly reserve, returns to the starting line-up to partner Liberian George Weah in attack after Marco Simone was ruled out with a stomach upset.
Milan also welcome back two players fundamental to their game -- sweeper and captain Franco Baresi and midfielder Demetrio Albertini.

Even more important for the champions perhaps is the current good form of Weah, scorer of five league goals and back in Italy after playing for Liberia in a 0-0 away draw with Zaire in the African Cup on Sunday.
Weah has an excellent record at Rome's Olympic Stadium, scoring decisive goals against both Roma and Lazio there in league wins last season.
Milan are currently second, just a point behind Juventus, a position Weah hopes to see improved.

"Milan is going to Rome to win. It won't be easy because Roma are in good form but we've got to give it a go," he said. "What interests me is that by Sunday night, we're on top of the table, on our own."
Stefano Eranio and Dutchman Edgar Davids are expected to replace Boban and Savicevic in the Milan midfield.
Roma, under new Argentine coach Carlos Bianchi, started the season determined to win the title for the first time since 1983.
One of five clubs in joint fourth, two points behind Milan, they have an embarrassment of strikers to choose from.
Argentine Abel Balbo and Francesco Totti will probably start the game with Uruguyan Daniel Fonseca and Marco Delvecchio on the bench.
In midfield Roma rely on the experience of Swede Jonas Thern alongside the emerging talent of 22-year-old Damiano Tommasi, while Brazilian Aldair and Argentine Roberto Trotta line up in defence.
Even though Saturday's game is going out on live pay-TV, more than 60,000 spectators are expected at the Olympic Stadium.
The game has been brought forward to Saturday because Roma play German side Karlsruhe in a UEFA Cup match on Tuesday.
